Documentation → Technical Reference → API library

API library and API packs

The API library is SATOM's database record of which endpoints and fields each exact firmware build serves, by REST and by CLI; signed API packs and knowledge packs — two lanes, each with its own key — carry that knowledge to nodes that cannot measure it themselves.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsregistry.edit appliances.apply users.manage
📍 WhereSoftware Update → API library packs (URL /self-update); API-Registry Explorer → Build / Harvest this appliance now (FortiWeb ADOM); Schema builds → Harvest (URL /schema-builds/); API Versions (/web/registry/versions); API field renames (/web/registry/field-map); shell: flask apilib, satom execute apipack

Overview#

Fortinet firmware builds differ in which REST endpoints and fields they serve — even builds of the same API version. The API library records, per product and per exact build, which endpoints and fields exist, their types and options, by which channel (REST, CLI or both), and the evidence each claim came from. It lives in the database (api_lib_* tables) and only ever grows: evidence outlives the appliance that produced it.

Pages that answer a firmware question read it: the API-Registry Explorer's Build panel and its pre-send check, the API Versions comparison, clone pre-flight and upgrade summaries. See API registry.

Evidence and verdicts#

Product Evidence sources
FortiWeb sweep (rediscovery of live appliances), schema (harvested field schemas), cli_tree, cli_full
FortiADC sweep (rediscovery of live appliances), schema (the harvest's read-only REST shape probe), legacy_matrix (frozen pre-build-axis data), cli_tree, cli_full (adapter verified on 7.6.7 build0676, {device}, 2026-10-13)
FortiAuthenticator schema — a read-only harvest of the device's own API schema (GET only); cli_tree, cli_full from its small setup CLI
FortiAnalyzer vendor_doc — the vendor's fortinet.fortianalyzer Ansible collection; schema — the per-object JSON-RPC syntax walk (get only), live from a registered FortiAnalyzer or by pack (adapter verified on 7.6.7 build3737); cli_tree by knowledge pack
FortiGate vendor_doc — fortinet.fortios; schema — the per-table ?action=schema read (GET only), live from a registered FortiGate or by pack; cli_tree by pack or import

When sources disagree the order is sweep > schema > cli_tree > cli_full > manual > legacy_matrix > vendor_doc. REST answers never read the two CLI sources.

Build status Meaning
measured A real appliance (or live schema read) produced evidence for this exact build
vendor_only Only vendor data covers the build — treat answers as claims
unmeasured No evidence; every endpoint is unknown, never "compatible"
unknown_firmware The appliance's firmware was never read

For one endpoint on one build the answer is measured (fields known), blind (answered, but no row showed its fields), unmeasured or absent (measured and not served). An error from the device is never read as "not served".

How the library grows#

Trigger What happens
A rediscovery sweep (FortiWeb, FortiADC) The sweep ingests its own snapshot
Firmware change detected by the firmware probe One background apilib_harvest job is queued if the new build has no evidence
API-Registry Explorer → Harvest this appliance now Same job for the selected appliance (appliances.apply). The Explorer belongs to the FortiWeb ADOM: it offers FortiWeb appliances only
Schema builds → Harvest For a FortiAnalyzer on a build with no harvested schema: the same syntax walk, stored as the same schema evidence — the on-demand harvest outside the FortiWeb ADOM
Scheduled action apilib_harvest Harvests every FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer whose build lacks healthy evidence — not scheduled by default
flask apilib harvest-fac Immediate FortiAuthenticator harvest
flask apilib import-vendor PATH Import an extracted vendor Ansible collection
Importing an API pack Adds evidence another node measured

At most one harvest per appliance is queued at a time; appliances in maintenance are not queued; a harvest cannot be stopped midway. Automatic dispatch can be turned off with the application setting APILIB_HARVEST_DISPATCH.

A FortiAnalyzer harvest reads the build from the box (get /sys/status), then asks the syntax of every /cli/global object the library and the registry name, one session, get only. It is healthy only when it read at least one object and no more than a quarter of the objects were refused (-11 is a refusal, never an absence); otherwise it is stored unhealthy with the reason and the build still needs a harvest. Measured on {device} (7.6.7 build3737): 165 requests in 6 s, 139 objects read, 11 absent, none refused; the children of tables with no row (23) cannot be asked and stay unmeasured.

The CLI channel#

The same build can serve a field over REST and the CLI, over one only, or only in show full-configuration. Two CLI sources record that, per exact build:

Source Read with Holds
cli_tree the CLI tree command the whole CLI schema: objects, fields, types, enum options, ranges, CLI attribute ids
cli_full show full-configuration the field names each object prints — never values

Both are keyed by the REST path (system/ntp/ntpserver), which is how they join the REST evidence. FortiAnalyzer is the exception: its CLI paths are its JSON-RPC URLs, and the tree a knowledge pack brings names an object system/admin.user/dashboard where the syntax walk says cli/global/system/admin/user/{user}/dashboard; SATOM derives the URL from each object's CLI path and enclosing tables so both meet on one object. A FortiADC tree from a knowledge pack is keyed the FortiWeb way too (load-balance/pool); SATOM re-keys it to the FortiADC REST path (load_balance_pool, <parent>_child_<table> for a nested table), and when the appliance's own harvest also covers the build, that record is the one read. From them, every field of a build gets a channel:

Channel Means
both REST and the CLI serve it
CLI only only the CLI has it
hidden only show full-configuration prints it
REST only REST serves it, the build's CLI schema does not list it
meta REST bookkeeping (id, _id, seq, q_*, sz_*, can_*, *_val; FortiADC _nondeletable, _noneditable), not configuration
unknown nothing measured it on that build — never read as "no"

A build is complete when nothing is unknown except named exceptions (licence, status-object). Measured: FortiWeb 7.6.8 and 8.0.6 have no CLI-only or hidden field at all; FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 has 29 CLI-only fields (its setup CLI) and 316 REST-only; FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7 has 1,494 fields served by both and 61 unknown (children of tables with no row, objects the build lacks); FortiADC 7.6.7 had 967 fields served by both before the measured renames below and has 1,082 with them.

ℹ️Note — FortiADC spells REST fields its own way

FortiADC's REST writes many CLI attributes with _ for - (direct_route_ip for direct-route-ip), calls the table key mkey, and renames some fields outright (pool for load-balance-pool). SATOM joins what the spelling proves and shows the field under its REST name. The outright renames are measured per build: on 7.6.7 ({device}, 115 renames) and 8.0.4 ({device}, 85 renames) each REST/CLI pair was kept only when the two values were equal on every row where both were printed, read-only (one REST GET per object and one show full-configuration). Those pairs are one field under the REST name (for example pool = load-balance-pool) and no longer read unverified on this build. A build that was not measured gets no renames — nothing is carried over from another build. A CLI field REST does not name, and that no measured rename covers, stays unknown. On FortiADC, CLI only therefore means REST answered 404 for the whole object.

Three features read the channels: Build compatibility, the Migration report and the CLI writer. New builds are detected and harvested from Schema builds.

⚠️Warning — Three lab findings every reader respects

  • FortiWeb answers an unserved nested path with its parent (HTTP 200 and the parent's rows). SATOM decides by the shape of the answer, never by the status.
  • show full-configuration prints conditionally: only fields that apply under a row's current settings. A field missing from a dump is not missing on the build.
  • REST silently ignores gated fields: a dependent field sent while its toggle is off answers 200 and is dropped. Send the toggle and its fields in one request; only a readback proves a write.

Harvesting the CLI channel#

  • API-Registry Explorer → Harvest CLI schema (appliances.apply, a device job, read-only on the box): tree, show full-configuration and one REST read per object the library has not measured.
  • Schema builds → Harvest for an appliance on a build with no harvested schema (one bell notification per new build).
  • Scheduled actions schema_harvest and schema_watch (not scheduled by default).
  • Shell: flask apilib schema-harvest <appliance>, flask apilib adapter-harvest <appliance>, sudo satom execute apilib harvest <appliance>.

Rename candidates#

Every CLI object and field carries an attribute id. On FortiWeb 7.6.8 → 8.0.6 the id was stable for 4,121 of 4,121 fields, and 18 renames were found by an equal id. SATOM shows such rename candidates; it never applies them. Only an operator rename map (below) is authoritative.

Field renames#

When a vendor renames a field between builds, the library would report "field removed + field added". API field renames (/web/registry/field-map, registry.edit) records that two names are one field. Mappings are never deleted, only retired, so the history of what was believed stays visible.

API packs#

An API pack (satom-apipack-<version>.tar.gz) carries API knowledge to a node — essential for offline nodes and for products the node has no appliance of. Since SATOM 3.0 every published pack is built by the SATOM team's Knowledge Harvester in two lanes with the same sections (schema satom.api-pack/2):

Lane Name Arrives
api_pack satom-apipack-<SATOM version>, pinned to that release inside the update
knowledge satom-apipack-kb-YYYYMMDD[.N], rolling from the knowledge feed or by upload — see Knowledge packs
Section Kind Imported into
library evidence the API library (sources sweep, schema, vendor_doc, cli_tree, cli_full, legacy_matrix)
docs release-notes, field-schemas, field-overlay the release-notes corpus, the field catalog, the FortiWeb field help
cli-coverage cli-coverage the CLI-only blocks per version (paths, set names and counts)
factory factory-wpp the factory catalog (predefined protection profiles per build)
field-map field-map rename candidates on API field renames — shown with a candidate badge, never applied
baselines baseline endpoint baselines as reference, only for a build with no baseline of this node's own, never the active one
signature-meta signature-meta public FortiGuard signature metadata (ships empty today)

Each payload is validated before anything is written; a malformed item is rejected with its reason and the rest still imports. A section or kind this SATOM does not know is skipped with a visible warning. A pack whose minimum SATOM version is newer than the node is refused whole.

A pack never carries configuration values or estate identity: device names become stable pseudonyms (witness-<hash>), serials and appliance ids are dropped, and a build is refused whole if a known device name, serial or appliance address survives.

Signing and import rules#

  • One key, one use. A 3.0 pack is verified only with the keys of its lane; a 2.x pack only with the update trust store; update packages never with a pack key. Unsigned, untrusted or altered packs are refused before anything is read. See Pack trust.
  • Local data always wins: what this node measured or wrote itself is never replaced. Between packs the newer snapshot wins whatever its lane; only when the snapshot time is unknown or equal does api_pack outrank knowledge. That is how corrections arrive.
  • Item states: new, update (replaces a copy an older pack wrote), present, local, rejected, unknown. Only new and update are imported.
  • Every imported row records its provenance — local, pack:api_pack:<pack> or pack:knowledge:<pack> — shown by inspect, the pack list and the import history.
  • Each import that changed something is logged in data/apipacks/imports/.
  • Import on the primary; a standby's database is read-only and gets the library by replication. On a standby the console refuses with "This node is the STANDBY — its database is read-only. Import the pack on the PRIMARY…"

How a node gets a pack#

Every release carries its own API pack in api-packs/ in the application tree. From 3.0 the release no longer carries a knowledge pack: those come from the feed or by upload (Knowledge packs).

Path Import
Installation (online or offline) The installer imports the release's pack after the health check (skip with SATOM_API_PACK=none; limit with SATOM_API_PACK_PRODUCTS)
Software update (git or offline package) The update runner imports the newest shipped pack on a primary or standalone node (turn off with SATOM_API_PACK_AUTO=0)
By hand Software Update → API library packs, or the CLI

A pack that fails to import is a warning, never a failed install or update.

Import from the console#

Requires users.manage (coarse user_manage).

  1. Open Software Update and scroll to API library packs.
  2. Pick a listed pack (this release marks the shipped one) or upload satom-apipack-<version>.tar.gz with Upload & check.
  3. Review the items and their states; filter by product or section.
  4. Tick the new and update items and click Import selected. The import runs as a background job with per-item progress.

Import from the shell#

satom show apipack                                    # packs on this node and the import log
sudo satom execute apipack import shipped             # dry run of the release's own pack
sudo satom execute apipack import shipped --yes       # import it
sudo satom execute apipack import ./satom-apipack-<version>.tar.gz --yes \
     --product fortiweb,fortiadc --section docs

The CLI runs the import as the service account and refuses on a standby.

Flask commands#

Run from /opt/satom as the service account: sudo -u satom env FLASK_APP=wsgi:app venv/bin/flask apilib …. Every command is safe to re-run (identical evidence only increments a confirmation counter). Errors print Error: … and exit 1.

Command Purpose
apilib status Counts per product, source and build
apilib backfill [--data-root DIR] [--product P]… Ingest every on-disk evidence store
apilib import-vendor PATH Import an extracted vendor Ansible collection (the directory holding MANIFEST.json)
apilib ingest-file PATH Ingest one evidence document (JSON, gzipped JSON or a list)
apilib harvest-fac [--appliance NAME] Harvest FortiAuthenticator schemas (GET only)
apilib schema-harvest APPLIANCE [--lab] [--no-probe] One appliance's CLI channel plus a REST probe of the paths the library lacks
apilib adapter-harvest APPLIANCE [--ssh-secret-env VAR] One appliance through its product's schema adapter
apilib schema-import --product fortigate\|fortianalyzer --version X [--tree F] [--schema F] Import saved schema captures
apilib compat PRODUCT BASE TARGET Two builds through both channels (JSON)
apilib channels PRODUCT BUILD One build, fields per channel (JSON)
apilib migration-report APPLIANCE --target BUILD [--backup ID] The migration report (JSON)
apilib baseline status Active endpoint baseline per product
apilib baseline promote --product P --build X [--apply] [--export] [--note] Promote what the library measured on build X as the registry baseline
apilib baseline adopt --product P --build X PATH [--note] One-time adoption of a legacy name→URN map
apilib baseline export [--product P] Write the active baselines to app/registry/baselines/
apilib baseline apply [--product P] Reconcile the registry to the active baseline (operator rows spared)
apilib baseline check [--product P] Drift report; exit 1 on drift
apilib baseline resolve --product P [--build X] NAME How NAME resolves on build X, and on what authority
apilib pack export --version V --out DIR [--product P]… [--section S]… [--notes] [--sign-key KEY] [--passphrase-file F] Build a legacy (/1) pack from this node's own measurements, for hand-over between nodes; unsigned unless --sign-key (a key the receiver trusts for updates). Releases no longer use it
apilib pack inspect PATH [--trust-dir DIR] Verify a pack and show what importing each item would do
apilib pack import PATH [--product P]… [--section S]… [--item ID]… [--dry-run] [--trust-dir DIR] Import the selected new items

Troubleshooting#

A build reads unmeasured#

Nothing measured it. For a FortiWeb use Harvest this appliance now in the Explorer; for a FortiAnalyzer, Schema builds → Harvest; for any registered FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate or FortiAnalyzer, run or schedule the apilib_harvest action. For a FortiGate or FortiAnalyzer build no appliance runs, import a newer vendor collection.

A FortiAnalyzer harvest fails: "the syntax walk read no object" or "… objects refused"#

The box answered but nothing was measured, or most objects answered -11. Check the admin's rpc-permit and its profile (the harvest only sends get), then harvest again. The unhealthy row is kept as the record of the failed read.

"Harvest not queued: …"#

The message names the reason: the product has no live harvester, the appliance is in maintenance, background harvest is switched off, or a harvest is already pending (then it is effectively queued — watch it in Jobs).

Pack import: no key in the trust store signed this package#

A 2.x pack whose signer is not in the update trust store. Install the public key with sudo satom execute trust add-key <key>.pub after comparing its fingerprint.

"this knowledge pack is not signed by a trusted knowledge key …"#

A 3.0 pack signed with another lane's key, with the release key, or by a key this node does not have for that lane. See Pack trust.

"pack … needs SATOM X or newer"#

The pack's minimum SATOM version is newer than this node. Update SATOM first; nothing was imported.

An item reads rejected or unknown#

rejected: its payload failed the checks of its kind (the reason is in the warning). unknown: a section this SATOM does not import yet. The rest of the pack imports either way.

Bell: "New build … schema not harvested"#

An appliance runs a build with no CLI schema in the library. Harvest it from Schema builds or import a knowledge pack that covers it.

Many fields read unknown after a harvest#

They belong to empty tables (or tables under a parent with no row): REST had nothing to read. Unknown is never absent; a knowledge pack with lab rows narrows it.

A pack item stays local#

Expected: this node measured that build itself, and local evidence always wins.

Advanced What the library replaced

The library replaced the file-based matrix (data/api_matrix/*.json), which was rebuilt wholesale and filtered through the live appliance list — deleting an appliance deleted the proof of what its firmware served. The JSON matrix still exists as an export for the offline CLI (satom get api versions, satom get api preflight), rebuilt from the API Versions page.

#api library#api pack#apipack#knowledge pack#lane#provenance#multi-build#factory#field map#signature meta#firmware build#evidence#harvest#sweep#schema#cli tree#show full-configuration#channel#hidden field#vendor collection#field map#baseline#flask apilib#offline

which keys ship, their fingerprints, and how to add or rotate one.Factory catalog (predefined Web Protection Profiles)The vendor-predefined FortiWeb Web Protection Profiles, stored once per firmware version, build and REST API version, so a deep rediscovery does not re-read them on every sweep; compare them between builds and save one as a template.Operator CLI (satom)The satom command-line console for the node itself — read state, run diagnostics and perform privileged repairs, updates and recoveries, even when the web interface is down.Offline update packagesUpdate a node with no route to the code repository — a signed package with the application and the Python wheels it may be missing, verified against a root-owned trust store and applied by the privileged runner with automatic rollback.Software UpdateUpdate SATOM's own code and Python dependencies — from the git remote or from a signed offline package — through a privileged runner, standby first on a pair.Product API pages (FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator)Each non-FortiWeb ADOM has its own API page that combines the product's endpoint catalog with a live console; this guide compares them and explains who may run write calls.Discovery and rediscoveryRead an appliance's entire configuration in one read-only sweep, refresh SATOM's cache and inventory from it, and optionally capture the full policy depth and the CLI configuration.InstallationHow to install a SATOM node — requirements and sizing, the connected and air-gapped (offline bundle) installs per distribution family, Docker, standalone or two-node cluster, what the installer sets up, and how to finish the install by arming the protections.
